runtime: C standard library, POSIX and the Windows API (system headers); callbacks are function-pointer typed
conventions: Symbols are C identifiers. Function pointer declarators and typedefs of them are function types (classified structurally); void * and variadic parameters are top types.

entries.describe: the loader calls a function marked __attribute__((constructor)) before main / when the library loads
entries.why: no call exists in source: the compiler places the function in the init array

entries.describe: the loader calls a function marked __attribute__((destructor)) at exit / when the library unloads
entries.why: no call exists in source: the compiler places the function in the fini array

io_send.describe: connect(fd, addr, len): outbound socket address (POSIX / Winsock)
sendto(fd, buf, len, flags, addr, addrlen): datagram to the address
execve(path, argv, envp) replaces the process with a program
execvp(file, argv) replaces the process with a program found on PATH
execv(path, argv) replaces the process with a program
posix_spawnp(pid, file, ...) starts a program found on PATH
system(command) runs a shell command line
popen(command, mode) runs a shell command line with a pipe
ShellExecuteW(hwnd, verb, file, ...) opens or runs a file (Windows)
WinHttpOpenRequest(connection, verb, object_name, ...) prepares an HTTP request (Windows)

io_entry.describe: accept(fd, ...): inbound connections of a server loop
recv(fd, ...): a consumer receive loop reads messages here
recvfrom(fd, ...): a consumer receive loop reads datagrams here

ffi_conventions.describe: JNI: an exported C function with this mangled name implements the Java native method
JNI RegisterNatives(env, class, methods, n): a JNINativeMethod table binds Java native method names to C functions
the JVM calls JNI_OnLoad when System.loadLibrary loads the library
CPython C-API: importing extension module <module> calls PyInit_<module>, which returns its PyModuleDef
CPython C-API: each {"name", c_function, flags} entry exposes c_function to Python as name
N-API: napi_create_function(env, name, len, cb, ...) exposes cb to JavaScript as name
N-API: NAPI_MODULE(name, init) registers the addon's init function
R: loading a package's shared library calls R_init_<package> (R_registerRoutines tables)
dlsym(handle, name) looks up an exported function by name
GetProcAddress(module, name) looks up an exported function by name (Windows)
clang wasm: the function is a wasm export named name
clang wasm: calls go to the host's import m.n

syntax_conventions.describe: DECLARE_NAPI_METHOD("name", fn) expands to a napi_property_descriptor that exports fn to JavaScript as name (the language server does not deliver the macro expansion)
NAPI_METHOD("name", fn) registers fn as the addon export name (macro expansion, not delivered by the language server)
